title: Bootstrap Theory of Representational Emergence: Explanatory Insufficiency as a Driver of Representation Learning and World Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.07303v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Representation learning is central to modern machine learning, yet most research focuses on optimizing representations after a representational framework has been selected. Less attention is given to when a new representational level becomes necessary. We introduce the Bootstrap Theory of Representational Emergence (TBER), a conceptual framework in which persistent explanatory insufficiency acts as a signal for representational transition. A representation may remain descriptively useful while becoming unable to make relevant observations, relations, transformations, or organizational properties intelligible. TBER describes a recursive five-stage process: stabilized observation, anomaly detection, recognition of explanatory insufficiency, representational emergence, and provisional stabilization. translated_title: 表征涌现的引导理论：解释不足作为表征学习与世界模型的驱动力
translated_abstract: 表征学习是现代机器学习的核心，但大多数研究在选定表征框架后专注于优化表征。较少关注何时需要新的表征层次。我们引入了表征涌现的引导理论（TBER），这是一个概念框架，其中持续的解释不足作为表征转换的信号。一个表征可能在保持描述性有用的同时，变得无法使相关观察、关系、转换或组织属性变得可理解。TBER描述了一个递归的五阶段过程：稳定观察、异常检测、解释不足识别、表征涌现和临时稳定。修订后的框架将涌现与验证区分开来：候选表征可能需要问题重新表征、判别性分析或进一步细化。
tldr: 该论文提出“表征涌现引导理论”，认为解释不足是驱动表征层级转换的关键信号，并描述了从稳定观察到表征涌现的递归五阶段过程。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Bootstrap Theory of Representational Emergence, proposing that explanatory insufficiency drives representational transitions through a recursive five-stage process.
